Summarize a diagnostic test

Source: R/dx_constructor.R
dx.Rd

Calculates diagnostic accuracy measures, with confidence intervals, for predicted probabilities compared to a binary reference standard: overall, at each threshold in threshold_range, and for each subgroup in grouping_variables.

Usage

dx(
  data,
  classlabels = c("Negative", "Positive"),
  threshold_range = NA,
  outcome_label = NA,
  pred_varname,
  true_varname,
  setthreshold = 0.5,
  poslabel = 1,
  grouping_variables = NA,
  prevalence = NA,
  citype = "exact",
  bootreps = 2000,
  bootseed = 20191015,
  doboot = FALSE,
  direction = "<",
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A tbl.

classlabels

Deprecated; has no effect.

threshold_range

Optional. A numeric vector of thresholds between 0 and 1 to loop over.

outcome_label

Deprecated; has no effect.

pred_varname

Column name containing the predictions (string). Values should be predicted probabilities that the outcome is 1, between 0 and 1, with no missing values.

true_varname

Column name containing the reference standard (string). Values should be 0 or 1 (numeric, logical, factor, or character), with no missing values, and both classes must be present.

setthreshold

A number between 0 and 1 representing the threshold used to classify the predictions

poslabel

The outcome class that is the event: 1 (default) or 0. Predictions are still probabilities that the outcome is 1, so with poslabel = 0 a prediction below the threshold is a positive test.

grouping_variables

Character vector of variable names to be summarized by. Variables are converted to factors if not already one. A column can't be named "Overall", which is used for the results of all cases.

prevalence

A single number greater than 0 and less than 1, representing a target prevalence for additional NPV and PPV calculations.

citype

Confidence interval type for proportions: one of the methods of binom::binom.confint(), such as "exact" (default), "wilson", or "ac". The estimate is always the observed proportion.

bootreps

Number of bootstrap samples used for the bootstrapped CIs.

bootseed

Seed used for the bootstrapped CIs, so results are reproducible on the same R version and platform. Bootstrap draws can differ across platforms and R versions by Monte Carlo error.

doboot

Logical. Generate percentile bootstrap CIs for the measures without a closed-form CI (F1, F2, MCC, balanced accuracy, informedness, markedness, G-mean, and Fowlkes-Mallows)? The confusion matrix cell counts are resampled from a multinomial distribution, which is equivalent to resampling cases.

direction

Deprecated. Predictions are probabilities that the outcome is 1, so higher predictions always point to outcome 1; use poslabel to choose which outcome is the event. Values other than the default, "<", give a warning and only affect the AUC and ROC curve (see ?pROC::roc). "auto" lets pROC choose the direction that gives an AUC of at least 0.5, which hides models that perform worse than chance.

...

currently unused

Value

An object of class "dx": a list with the data, the options used, the measures at each threshold and subgroup (measures), measures across all thresholds (thresholds), a prevalence analysis (prevalence), the ranked predictions used by the gain, lift, KS, and CAP plots (rank), the confusion matrix at setthreshold (cm), and the pROC::roc() object (roc). Use summary.dx() or as.data.frame.dx() to view the measures.

Examples

dx_obj <- dx(
  data = dx_heart_failure,
  true_varname = "truth",
  pred_varname = "predicted",
  setthreshold = .3,
  grouping_variables = c("AgeGroup", "Sex")
)
summary(dx_obj)

# Bootstrapped CIs for measures without a closed-form CI
dx_boot <- dx(
  data = dx_heart_failure,
  true_varname = "truth",
  pred_varname = "predicted",
  setthreshold = .3,
  doboot = TRUE,
  bootreps = 500
)
summary(dx_boot, measure = c("F1 Score", "Matthews Correlation Coefficient"))
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Threshold= 0.3
#> 
#> |variable |label   |measure                          |summary           |
#> |:--------|:-------|:--------------------------------|:-----------------|
#> |Overall  |Overall |F1 Score                         |0.75 (0.68, 0.82) |
#> |Overall  |Overall |Matthews Correlation Coefficient |0.59 (0.48, 0.68) |
